Question Choices: Select. What does a left-tailed distribution look like? ~~Tail-to-the-right | Tail-to-the-left | No-tail | Equal-sides~~
Hints: Follow the long tail, not the location of the peak.
Solution: A left-tailed or left-skewed distribution has its longer tail extending toward smaller values on the left. Name the direction of the tail, not the tall bars.

Question Choices: What is a peak? (A) Lowest value   (B) Most frequent value area   (C) Gap   (D) Outlier
Hints: Distinguish nearby groups, empty intervals, high-frequency areas, and isolated values.
Solution: B. A peak is a locally high frequency area of a distribution. A distribution can have more than one peak; it does not mean the largest data value.

Question Choices: Which statement is TRUE?  (A) A cluster means no data   (B) A gap means no data in a range   (C) A peak means smallest value   (D) Outlier is always the median
Hints: Distinguish nearby groups, empty intervals, high-frequency areas, and isolated values.
Solution: B. A gap is an interval containing no observations. A cluster contains nearby observations, a peak has locally high frequency, and an outlier is unusually far from the others.

Question Choices: Select. A graph is symmetrical. Which relationship follows from symmetry?: ~~Mean=median(approximately) | Has-a-long-tail | Has-an-outlier | Has-a-gap~~
Hints: Think of equal frequencies balancing at equal distances from the center.
Solution: For exactly symmetric finite data, equal distances on either side balance about the center, so mean and median coincide. For an approximately symmetric distribution they are often close. Symmetry alone does not require a tail, gap, or outlier.

Question Choices: Select. A distribution has many values around 30 and a few very large values (>30). What shape is it? ~~Symmetrical | Left-skewed | Right-skewed | No-pattern~~
Hints: Follow the long tail, not the location of the peak.
Solution: A tail extending toward larger values on the right gives a right-tailed or right-skewed distribution.
